The '''DH-17 blaster pistol''' was a ranged weapon produced by [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech Industries]] and used primarily for shipboard combat.

==Description==
The DH-17 was a long-nosed [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]], weighing approximately one [[Kilogram/Legends|kilogram]].<ref name="FF106" /> The [[gas chamber]] on the DH-17 held enough [[Blaster gas/Legends|blaster gas]] for five hundred shots before needing to be refilled, while the [[Blaster power pack/Legends|power pack]] only held enough power for one hundred shots. Due to the weapon's design, experienced [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] could reload a weapon in around five [[Standard second|seconds]]. Power packs that had been fired until they were empty could be recharged in fifteen [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]].<ref name="EGWT" />

Designed for short range combat, the DH-17 had a optimal range of thirty [[Meter/Legends|meters]], although its maximum range was one hundred and twenty meters. The blaster was designed for semiautomatic fire, discharging a bolt once for every trigger pull. The DH-17 could be converted to fire in a fully automatic mode, although the modification had the downside of draining the power pack in twenty seconds. In addition, the excessive heat generated by the fire rate could melt the blaster's internal components and even cause the weapon to overload and explode.<ref name="EGWT" />

[[File:DH17blaster-NEGWT.png|thumb|left|180px|DH-17 blaster pistol]]
The weapon's energy bolts could punch through [[Stormtrooper armor/Legends|stormtrooper armor]] and low-level [[Force field/Legends|force fields]], although it stopped short of being able to puncture the [[Hull/Legends|hull]] of a [[Starship/Legends|starship]]. As a result, the DH-17 was favored by troops stationed aboard ships. The blaster's [[Stun/Legends|stun]] setting was capable of rendering a [[Human/Legends|Human]] unconscious for around ten [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]].<ref name="EGWT" /> 

The [[targeting scope]] on the DH-17 had a 2x zoom with 50 [[Centimeter/Legends|centimeters]] of eye relief. It had 90% light transmission and could display range and power settings on a built-in display.<ref name="BP" />

DH-17 blaster pistols were sold for between five hundred and fifty<ref name="FF106" /> and eight hundred [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]],<ref name="SESB" /> although prices on the [[Black market/Legends|black market]] varied considerably.<ref name="FF106" /> During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], BlasTech produced variants of the DH-17, including the [[DH-17 blaster carbine/Legends|DH-17 blaster carbine]] and [[DH-17 short carbine]].<ref name="Galaxies">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>

==History==
The DH-17 blaster pistol was considered to be a workhorse of a pistol, with unmatched popularity and staying power. When released by [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech Industries]], the weapon was hailed as a considerable improvement over previous weapon designs by both the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and local [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement agencies]].<ref name="FF106" /> During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the DH-17 was the standard sidearm used by both the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance]] [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]]. It remained popular with [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] personnel.<ref name="EGWT" />

[[File:DH17_egwt.png|thumb|right|180px|DH-17 [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]]]]
[[Rebel trooper/Legends|Rebel troopers]] were commonly armed with DH-17 pistols. The crew of the ''[[Tantive IV/Legends|Tantive IV]]'' were armed with DH-17s, and used them in the failed attempt to prevent Imperial forces led by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] from capturing the vessel.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> Rebel forces assigned to [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on the ice [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] were also armed with the weapon.<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref>

[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] was also commonly seen with the DH-17,<ref name="FF106" /> and a weapon of this type was also carried as a sidearm by [[Chak Fel]] on the mission to [[Outbound Flight Project|Outbound Flight]] in [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]] as a representative of the [[Empire of the Hand]].<ref name="SQ">''[[Survivor's Quest]]''</ref>

The weapon was illegal for civilian ownership, restricted to possession by military personnel of both the Galactic Empire and New Republic.<ref name="EGWT" /> Owners were required to license their weapons;<ref name="FF106" /> however, the weapons were widely available on the [[Black market/Legends|black market]]<ref name="EGWT" /> and used extensively by [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] and [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] gangs.<ref name="FF106" />

Newer blasters, such as the [[DL-18 Blaster Pistol]] and the [[DH-23 blaster pistol/Legends|DH-23 'Outback']] were released by BlasTech, hoping to capitalize on the success of the DH-17. Despite design improvements, neither of the weapons came close to overcoming the marketing dominance of the DH-17. Soldiers and outlaws continued to use the DH-17 which served as a testament to the superb performance and craftsmanship of the weapon.<ref name="FF106" />

==Behind the scenes==
The DH-17 prop was made using the same [[Wikipedia:Sterling submachine gun|Sterling L2A3 sub-machine gun]] used for the [[E-11]], with a different barrel housing. The prop in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']] was not usable for actual firing and was primarily only a cast. In some scenes on the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], such as the Detention Block scene, the officers carry DH-17 props until they begin to fire, where the weapons turn into E-11s. For [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']] the DH-17s were made off of real Sterlings and were usable props that could actually fire. Despite the prop upgrade, the weapon had very little overall screen time during the film.
